fixed.explanation: TryPushdownPrefixFilter only recognized a function named "prefix". The starts_with function and the ^@ operator are most likely registered under the name "starts_with", so they never reached the range-pushdown path. The edit accepts all three names, so the existing code emits s >= prefix AND s < next_prefix and zone maps can prune. It also adds a NULL constant guard. I couldn't see the function registration, so the "starts_with" name is inferred from the issue's plans and not checked.

query.intent: Optimizer rule that rewrites LIKE 'prefix%' into range comparisons (s >= 'prefix' AND s < 'prefix+1') for filter pushdown and row group pruning should also handle starts_with(s, 'prefix') and the prefix operator ^@, which are currently left as opaque filters.
query.symptom: starts_with(s, 'x') and s ^@ 'x' filters are not converted into range filters so zone-map pruning scans all row groups, unlike LIKE 'x%'.

history.analysis: FilterCombiner::TryPushdownPrefixFilter handles starts_with and prefix (^@). It pushes an opaque expression filter and gives no range bounds, so zone maps can't prune. TryPushdownLikeFilter produces the (s >= x AND s < x+1) range filters that do prune. The fix is probably to make the prefix pushdown also emit range comparisons, as the LIKE path does. I did not see the full bodies of these functions.
